title: OpenFerro: a unified framework for mesoscale ferroic dynamics and enhanced sampling
abstractExcerpt: Modeling ferroic materials requires connecting microscopic fluctuations to collective dynamics over mesoscales. We introduce OpenFerro, a unified lattice-field dynamics framework that combines flexible Hamiltonians, automatic differentiation, parallel execution, and enhanced sampling. The same framework can simulate ferroelectric domain motion, magnetic disordering, and coupled spin-lattice thermodynamics. On four graphics processors, a bulk BaTiO$_3$ benchmark with long-range dipolar interaction reaches $840^3$ unit cells, representing 3 billion atoms through the retained lattice variables.

abstractExcerpt: Proteins in solution often populate conformational ensembles that differ from the static states captured by crystallography or AI-based structure prediction. Conventional molecular dynamics (MD) simulations often fail to cross the energy barriers separating these states on accessible timescales, and statistical reweighting cannot recover conformations never sampled. abstractExcerpt: Many molecular dynamics simulations aim at studying transitions between two states (from reactants to products). title: Torsional selection rule for the spin--orbit conversion of light

openalex.subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics

abstractExcerpt: Standard Pancharatnam-Berry and linear-birefringent media convert optical spin into orbital angular momentum (OAM) through an anisotropy \emph{director}, a rank-two, headless field, and therefore obey the selection rule $Δ\ell=2q$ per unit texture charge $q$. We show that a medium with geometric \emph{torsion}, the continuum limit of a screw-dislocation array, can convert spin to OAM through the \emph{contortion} of its material connection, which enters the effective paraxial dynamics as a rank-one vector field. The resulting selection rule is $Δ\ell=q$.

title: Machine Learning as a Lens for Breaking Scaling Relations in Heterogeneous Catalysis: Strategies, Evidence, and Limits

stories.title: AI-Designed Enzymes: Powering Catalysis with Machine Learning

abstractExcerpt: Linear scaling relations and the Sabatier principle impose a fundamental ceiling on the activity of heterogeneous catalysts: because the binding energies of related intermediates are coupled, optimising one weakens another, and the best catalyst sits at a volcano apex rather than beyond it. A fast-growing literature claims that machine learning (ML) can identify catalysts that break these relations. This review asks a deliberately sceptical question: does ML genuinely reveal scaling-relation violations, or are many reported “escapes” modelling artefacts of small DFT datasets and overfitting?

abstractExcerpt: Organisms and their enzymes adapt to environmental temperatures, such that thermophilic enzymes exhibit high melting and optimum temperatures while psychrophilic enzymes exhibit low values for both. title: Engineering high-titer lentiviral vectors for robust expression of RNA-based gene circuits
abstractExcerpt: Lentiviral vectors enable efficient delivery of genetic cargoes for gene and cell therapies. With their [~]10-kb packaging limit, lentiviral vectors can encode multiple transcription units, supporting delivery of compact gene circuits. RNA-based devices offer highly compact control including ligand-responsive induction and closed-loop regulation. However, RNA devices such as ribozymes and splicing switches may interfere with vector production via activity on the single-stranded RNA genome.
